lesson_title: One Note, Five Checkpoints: Profitability Percentages
hook_text: Follow one R100 note out of the till. Watch who takes a cut.
clip_script: Take one hundred-rand note out of the till — and follow it as it breaks up. A customer hands it over for goods. First, the goods must be replaced: sixty-six rand seventy goes straight back into stock — that's the cost under a fifty percent mark-up. Thirty-three rand thirty remains — the margin, the money the shop actually gets to work with. Then the running of the shop takes its share: wages, electricity, insurance, the stock that went missing — about twenty-five rand of every hundred. The loan's interest nibbles its two rand fifty. And when every taker has taken... seventeen rand fifty remains. From every single hundred that crossed the counter, the owner keeps seventeen-fifty. That journey — a hundred in, sixty-seven replaced, thirty-three margin, twenty-five running, seventeen-fifty kept — IS profitability analysis. The five official percentages are just checkpoint names along the note's journey. And rand totals are trapped in their own year; percentages travel — compare them with last year, with the shop across the road, with anyone. That's how numbers learn to talk.
visual_style: A single glowing R100 note travelling a conveyor through the shop, pieces splitting off at labelled checkpoints (66,70 / 33,30 / 25,30 / 17,50), the fragments assembling into a dashboard of five percentages at the end.
mood: Follow-the-money documentary energy, crisp and revelatory.
pacing: Continuous tracking motion with a beat at each split, closing on the dashboard snap.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and make your own numbers talk.
